DIAGNOSIS READY: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu Syndrome)

The blood tests and coagulation profiles are completely normal, which rules out common causes like leukemia or clotting factor deficiencies. Given your normal platelet count and normal clotting times combined with spontaneous nosebleeds and petechiae, we need to examine your oral cavity for characteristic telangiectasias (small, persistent blood vessels) on your lips, tongue, or inside your cheeks. Can you describe if you have any family history of frequent bleeding or nosebleeds? REQUEST IMAGES: Oral_Cavity_Inspection
